rulings.challenge_claim: The rejected_alternative rebuts only a weak 'gap-free YHWH-token run' rival and omits the strongest real rival: a byte-verified lev/adam inclusio bracketing the 15:33-16:9 span the row discusses.
rulings.grounds: Re-derived independently from verse_map_oshb.json (direct file splice, byte tier): oshb:Prov.16.1 opens "לְאָדָ֥ם מַֽעַרְכֵי לֵ֑ב" (adam...lev order) and oshb:Prov.16.9 opens "לֵ֣ב אָ֭דָם" (lev...adam order) -- collate.py confirmed byte tier on the 16:1 quote; the 16:9 quote lost one cantillation mark in shell argv transit (the TOOLKIT's documented shell-transit hazard) and registered accent_stripped, but the direct file splice is byte-exact and the lexeme order is unambiguous. This is a genuine chiastic lev/adam inclusio bracketing 16:1-16:9, independently corroborated by the writer's own disclosures at the bracket rows: P07-030 (16:1) calls it a 'non-adjacent inclusio with 16:9' and P07-038 (16:9) calls it 'the non-adjacent lev/adam/YHWH inclusio noted there' (both rows out of this cluster's scope, cited only as corroboration, not re-ruled). P07-034 (16:5, interior to the bracket) is the row that discusses the 15:33-16:9 span in its own rejected_alternative, yet engages only the weaker gap-free-YHWH-run rival, which the row's own citations show is already dead on arrival once 16:8's lack of any divine-name token is noted -- not the inclusio, which is the strongest real rival for that span. Upheld at the tier LF names (medium): the underlying single_proverb call for 16:5 is not disturbed -- independent token comparison across all six adjacent pairs 16:1/16:2 through 16:6/16:7 (byte-spliced from verse_map_oshb.json; see the P07-031/032/033/035/036 rulings below) shows the interior verses 16:2-16:7 share no content token beyond the bare divine name, so the inclusio alone does not extend cluster-level cohesion to 16:5 -- but the row's rejected_alternative fails the strongest-rival test as written.
rulings.remedy: Work order (field: rejected_alternative, P07-034/Prov.16.5): replace the engaged rival. The primary sentence should reject a 16:1-16:9 envelope-unit reading grounded in the lev/adam chiastic inclusio (oshb:Prov.16.1 "לְאָדָ֥ם...לֵ֑ב" vs oshb:Prov.16.9 "לֵ֣ב אָ֭דָם", collate.py byte tier), stating that the interior verses 16:2-16:7 share no uniform construction or content token with either bracket beyond the bare divine name, so the inclusio does not itself extend cluster-level cohesion to this row. The gap-free-YHWH-run point may survive only as the optional second sentence, if at all. Test the cure must pass: the revised sentence must name the inclusio, not the YHWH-run, as the rebutted rival. Any implication that 16:1-16:9 (or a sub-span) should become a proverb_cluster given the inclusio is a boundary-adoption question for the boss round, not settled by this ruling.

rulings.challenge_claim: The claimed distance between 16:6's yirat-YHWH phrase and 15:33's is arithmetically wrong: six verses later, not seven.
rulings.grounds: Direct count from Prov.15.33 to Prov.16.6 (16:1, 16:2, 16:3, 16:4, 16:5, 16:6) is six elapsed verses, not seven. The underlying phrase-echo claim is accurate and unaffected: oshb:Prov.15.33 "יִרְאַ֣ת יְ֭הוָה" and oshb:Prov.16.6 "וּבְיִרְאַ֥ת יְ֝הוָ֗ה" byte-match the same construct phrase (direct splice from verse_map_oshb.json), and its texture-not-driver treatment is correct. Only the digit in observed_substrate_signals is wrong. Convergence note: distinct from the OL challenge on this same row below (an evidentiary-tier defect in the rejected_alternative field, not this arithmetic slip in observed_substrate_signals) -- both primaries hit P07-035 but on separate defects, not a duplicate.
rulings.remedy: Work order (field: observed_substrate_signals, P07-035/Prov.16.6): change "seven lines earlier" to "six lines earlier." Test the cure must pass: a direct re-count of the 15:33-to-16:6 verse span.

rulings.challenge_claim: The 16:6 rejected_alternative's 'no other token repeats' claim against 16:5 is given only in transliteration, unswept (check_universals.py class).
rulings.grounds: Independently re-derived (not taken on OL's word): byte-spliced oshb:Prov.16.5 "תּוֹעֲבַ֣ת יְ֭הוָה כָּל גְּבַהּ לֵ֑ב יָ֥ד לְ֝יָ֗ד לֹ֣א יִנָּקֶֽה" and oshb:Prov.16.6 "בְּחֶ֣סֶד וֶ֭אֱמֶת יְכֻפַּ֣ר עָוֺ֑ן וּבְיִרְאַ֥ת יְ֝הוָ֗ה ס֣וּר מֵרָֽע" from verse_map_oshb.json (byte tier): token sets share exactly one item, יהוה. The row's underlying claim is correct but stated in transliteration only, with no Hebrew quoted and no digit-bearing sweep citation -- the defect class check_universals.py's negative-universal lexicon exists to catch. Convergence note: distinct from the LF item on this same row above (an arithmetic slip in a different field).
rulings.remedy: See the class-level remedy specified under the P07-031 ruling in this same attempt: this row's rejected_alternative is one of the five rows folded into that single sweep, not patched individually.

rulings.challenge_claim: The decision to keep 16:2 separate from 16:1 rests on a Hebrew no-shared-token claim given only in transliteration, with no quoted Hebrew for collate.py to check.
rulings.grounds: Independently re-derived: byte-spliced oshb:Prov.16.1 "לְאָדָ֥ם מַֽעַרְכֵי לֵ֑ב וּ֝מֵיְהוָ֗ה מַעֲנֵ֥ה לָשֽׁוֹן" and oshb:Prov.16.2 "כָּֽל דַּרְכֵי אִ֭ישׁ זַ֣ךְ בְּעֵינָ֑יו וְתֹכֵ֖ן רוּח֣וֹת יְהוָֽה" from verse_map_oshb.json (byte tier): shared token set = {יהוה} only. The row's decision and underlying claim both stand -- but the claim is presented in transliteration only, failing the campaign's Hebrew-quote-plus-digit-sweep bar for a negative universal.
rulings.remedy: Work order -- ONE class-level Hebrew-engagement sweep over writer/p07_rows.jsonl (not five individual patches): for every row whose rejected_alternative or observed_substrate_signals carries a 'no other/no repeated token' (or equivalent negative-universal) claim stated only in transliteration -- this row (16:1/16:2), P07-032 (16:2/16:3), P07-033 (16:3/16:4), P07-035 (16:5/16:6), and P07-036 (16:6/16:7) -- splice the paired verses' pointed Hebrew from verse_map_oshb.json into the row at byte tier, and attach the digit-bearing sweep result (shared-token-count = 1, the bare divine name, in every one of these five pairs). Run check_universals.py over the full revised part in one pass and confirm zero unswept-universal flags remain before closing the class; do not close rows individually. Test the cure must pass: check_universals.py clean re-run on p07_rows.jsonl.

rulings.challenge_claim: The 16:3 rejected_alternative's 'no other token is shared' claim against 16:2 is asserted in transliteration only, with no sweep citation (check_universals.py flag).
rulings.grounds: Independently re-derived: byte-spliced oshb:Prov.16.2 "כָּֽל דַּרְכֵי אִ֭ישׁ זַ֣ךְ בְּעֵינָ֑יו וְתֹכֵ֖ן רוּח֣וֹת יְהוָֽה" and oshb:Prov.16.3 "גֹּ֣ל אֶל יְהוָ֣ה מַעֲשֶׂ֑יךָ וְ֝יִכֹּ֗נוּ מַחְשְׁבֹתֶֽיךָ": shared token set = {יהוה} only (וְתֹכֵ֖ן, root t-k-n, and וְ֝יִכֹּ֗נוּ, root k-w-n, are phonetically similar but consonantally distinct roots, not a shared token). Decision stands; presentation fails the Hebrew-quote-plus-digit-sweep bar, same class as P07-031.
rulings.remedy: Folded into the ONE class-level sweep specified under the P07-031 ruling in this same attempt; not patched individually.

rulings.challenge_claim: The 16:7 rejected_alternative's claim that it and 16:6 share no token beyond YHWH is given only in transliteration with no sweep citation -- the same defect class as the other rows even though check_universals.py's literal lexicon missed this phrasing.
rulings.grounds: Independently re-derived: byte-spliced oshb:Prov.16.6 "בְּחֶ֣סֶד וֶ֭אֱמֶת יְכֻפַּ֣ר עָוֺ֑ן וּבְיִרְאַ֥ת יְ֝הוָ֗ה ס֣וּר מֵרָֽע" and oshb:Prov.16.7 "בִּרְצ֣וֹת יְ֭הוָה דַּרְכֵי אִ֑ישׁ גַּם א֝וֹיְבָ֗יו יַשְׁלִ֥ם אִתּֽוֹ": shared token set = {יהוה} only. The decision, and the separate darkhe-ish cross-cite to 16:2, both stand; presentation fails the Hebrew-quote-plus-digit-sweep bar. OL is right that this is the identical defect class to the check_universals.py-flagged rows even though the tool's literal lexicon ('no other'/'no X') did not match this row's 'otherwise share no token' phrasing.
rulings.remedy: Folded into the ONE class-level sweep specified under the P07-031 ruling in this same attempt; not patched individually. Separately (tool-owner note, not a row remedy): check_universals.py's negative-universal lexicon should be widened to catch 'X and Y share/carry no token' phrasing, not just 'no other'/'no X.'
